# kube-dump

## NAME

**kube-dump** - Save, read, inspect, and encrypt Kubernetes backup artifacts.

## SYNOPSIS

`kube-dump [OPTIONS]`

## DESCRIPTION

kube-dump saves Kubernetes resources, PVC data, and container images.

Use resource, pvc, and image commands to work with each artifact type.
Profiles control resource selection and cleanup; encryption is applied only when explicitly configured.

### key

Generate age identities and maintain AES-SIV keyrings

Create a native age identity or maintain the AES-SIV keyring stored inside a local backup directory.

Keyring maintenance works only with an existing local directory or Git worktree. It does not access S3, rewrite resource manifests, or re-encrypt existing resource fields automatically. Use download or extract first when the keyring is stored in a remote or archive backend.

The generate command creates only a native age X25519 identity. Rotate changes the active AES-SIV key and keeps historical keys. Rewrap changes only the age protection around existing AES-SIV keys. Both maintenance commands require an authorized private identity and at least one new age recipient.

**Usage:** `kube-dump [OPTIONS] key`

#### Examples

```text
kube-dump key generate
```

### key generate

Generate a native age X25519 identity

Create a native age X25519 identity for encrypting resource fields, archives, and AES-SIV keyrings.

The private identity is written to standard output unless `--output` is specified. The output file is created with private-file permissions and is never overwritten. This command does not create SSH identities, AES-SIV keyrings, or passphrase-protected identity files.

**Usage:** `kube-dump [OPTIONS] key generate [generate-OPTIONS]`

#### Examples

```text
kube-dump key generate --output age-identity.txt
```

#### Output

|Option|Description|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|
|`-o`, `--output`|Write the identity to this file; default: standard output|`$KUBE_DUMP_OUTPUT`|no|

### key rewrap

Re-encrypt AES-SIV key envelopes for new age recipients

Replace every age-encrypted AES-SIV key envelope in an existing local backup keyring.

The AES-SIV keys and encrypted resource values do not change. Only their age envelopes are rewritten for the recipients supplied by recipient flags. The current private age identity is required to read all existing envelopes, including historical keys retained after rotation.

The DIRECTORY must contain `.kube-dump/crypto/metadata.yaml`. This command does not modify resource manifests or operate directly on S3 and archive backends.

**Usage:** `kube-dump [OPTIONS] key rewrap [rewrap-OPTIONS]`

#### Examples

```text
kube-dump key rewrap ./backup -i age-identity.txt -R age1example
```

#### Encryption

|Option|Description|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|
|`--identity-passphrase`|Passphrase for an encrypted SSH identity|`$KUBE_DUMP_IDENTITY_PASSPHRASE`|no|
|`--identity-passphrase-file`|Read the passphrase for an encrypted SSH identity from this file|`$KUBE_DUMP_IDENTITY_PASSPHRASE_FILE`|no|
|`-i`, `--identity`|Age identity file used to decrypt archives, fields, or keyrings|`$KUBE_DUMP_IDENTITY` (`,`)|no|
|`-R`, `--recipient`|Age recipient used for encryption|`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENT` (`,`)|no|
|`--recipients-file`|File containing age recipients|`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENTS_FILE` (`,`)|no|
|`--recipients-url`|HTTP or HTTPS URL containing age recipients|`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENTS_URL` (`,`)|no|
|`--recipient-github-user`|GitHub username whose public SSH keys provide age recipients|`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENT_GITHUB_USER` (`,`)|no|

#### Arguments

|Name|Description|Required|
|---|---|---|
|`DIRECTORY`|Local backup directory or Git worktree|yes|

### key rotate

Rotate the active AES-SIV key in a local keyring

Create a new AES-SIV data key and make it active in an existing local backup keyring.

The current private age identity is required to open the keyring, and recipient flags supply the age recipients for the new envelope. Historical AES-SIV keys remain in the keyring, so existing encrypted values stay readable. Resource manifests are not rewritten; use resource encrypt when that is required.

The DIRECTORY must contain `.kube-dump/crypto/metadata.yaml`. Remote S3 objects and standalone archives must be downloaded or extracted to a local directory before this command can use them.

**Usage:** `kube-dump [OPTIONS] key rotate [rotate-OPTIONS]`

#### Examples

```text
kube-dump key rotate ./backup -i age-identity.txt -R age1example
```

#### Encryption

|Option|Description|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|
|`--identity-passphrase`|Passphrase for an encrypted SSH identity|`$KUBE_DUMP_IDENTITY_PASSPHRASE`|no|
|`--identity-passphrase-file`|Read the passphrase for an encrypted SSH identity from this file|`$KUBE_DUMP_IDENTITY_PASSPHRASE_FILE`|no|
|`-i`, `--identity`|Age identity file used to decrypt archives, fields, or keyrings|`$KUBE_DUMP_IDENTITY` (`,`)|no|
|`-R`, `--recipient`|Age recipient used for encryption|`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENT` (`,`)|no|
|`--recipients-file`|File containing age recipients|`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENTS_FILE` (`,`)|no|
|`--recipients-url`|HTTP or HTTPS URL containing age recipients|`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENTS_URL` (`,`)|no|

#### Arguments

|---|---|---|
|`DIRECTORY`|Local backup directory or Git worktree|yes|

### pvc

Capture and restore files stored in PersistentVolumeClaims

Read PVC filesystems through Kubernetes, store each claim as a portable compressed archive, and inspect, transfer, encrypt, decrypt, or extract those archives.

**Usage:** `kube-dump [OPTIONS] pvc [pvc-OPTIONS]`

#### Examples

```text
kube-dump pvc save dir ./pvc-data
```

#### Capture and restore files stored in PersistentVolumeClaims

|---|---|---|---|---|

### pvc restore

Restore a saved PVC archive into an existing PVC

Restore one selected PVC artifact into an already created target PVC. The target must be Bound, use Filesystem mode, be unused, and have capacity at least as large as the uncompressed archive payload. The default empty-only policy refuses to overwrite existing data; use `--existing` merge or replace explicitly.

**Usage:** `kube-dump [OPTIONS] pvc [pvc-OPTIONS] restore`

#### Examples

```text
kube-dump pvc restore dir ./pvc-data
```

### pvc restore dir

Restore a local PVC archive into an existing PVC

Select a saved PVC artifact by source identity and revision, then stream its decrypted and decompressed contents into the target PVC.

**Usage:** `kube-dump [OPTIONS] pvc [pvc-OPTIONS] restore dir [dir-OPTIONS]`

#### Examples

```text
kube-dump pvc restore dir ./pvc-data --pvc production/postgres-data --target-pvc recovery/postgres-data
```

#### Restore

|Option|Description|Default|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|`--pvc`|Saved source PVC as NAMESPACE/NAME||`$KUBE_DUMP_PVC`|yes|
|`--target-pvc`|Existing target PVC as NAMESPACE/NAME||`$KUBE_DUMP_TARGET_PVC`|yes|
|`--revision`|Artifact timestamp or latest|`latest`|`$KUBE_DUMP_REVISION`|no|
|`--existing`|Policy for existing target data; choices: `empty-only, merge, replace`|`empty-only`|`$KUBE_DUMP_EXISTING`|no|

#### PVC

|Option|Description|Default|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|`--image`|Container image used by the PVC helper Pod||`$KUBE_DUMP_IMAGE`|no|
|`--image-pull-policy`|Pull policy for temporary PVC helper Pods; choices: `Always, IfNotPresent, Never`|`IfNotPresent`|`$KUBE_DUMP_IMAGE_PULL_POLICY`|no|
|`--helper-binary-path`|Path to the volume agent inside the helper container; default: kube-dump from PATH, then /kube-dump||`$KUBE_DUMP_HELPER_BINARY_PATH`|no|

#### Encryption

|Option|Description|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|
|`--identity-passphrase`|Passphrase for an encrypted SSH identity|`$KUBE_DUMP_IDENTITY_PASSPHRASE`|no|
|`--identity-passphrase-file`|Read the passphrase for an encrypted SSH identity from this file|`$KUBE_DUMP_IDENTITY_PASSPHRASE_FILE`|no|
|`-i`, `--identity`|Age identity file used to decrypt archives, fields, or keyrings|`$KUBE_DUMP_IDENTITY` (`,`)|no|

#### Arguments

|Name|Description|Required|
|---|---|---|
|`PATH`|PVC artifact directory|yes|

### pvc save

Capture PVC filesystems as compressed archives

Read selected PVC filesystems through the configured strategy and store one compressed artifact per claim in a new timestamped directory. Artifacts are grouped by namespace and PVC; keep the latest per PVC with `--keep`. Use `--keep` 0 to disable rotation.

**Usage:** `kube-dump [OPTIONS] pvc [pvc-OPTIONS] save`

#### Examples

```text
kube-dump pvc save dir ./pvc-data
```

### pvc save dir

Capture PVC filesystems and store archives locally

**Usage:** `kube-dump [OPTIONS] pvc [pvc-OPTIONS] save dir [dir-OPTIONS]`

#### Profile

|Option|Description|Default|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|`--profile-dir`|Directory containing global profiles||`$KUBE_DUMP_PROFILE_DIR`|no|
|`-p`, `--profile`|Profile name, builtin:name, global:name, or YAML file|`backup`|`$KUBE_DUMP_PROFILE`|no|

#### Encryption

|Option|Description|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|
|`-R`, `--recipient`|Age recipient used for encryption|`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENT` (`,`)|no|
|`--recipients-file`|File containing age recipients|`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENTS_FILE` (`,`)|no|
|`--recipients-url`|HTTP or HTTPS URL containing age recipients|`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENTS_URL` (`,`)|no|
|`--recipient-github-user`|GitHub username whose public SSH keys provide age recipients|`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENT_GITHUB_USER` (`,`)|no|

#### PVC

|Option|Description|Default|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|`--image`|Container image used by the PVC helper Pod||`$KUBE_DUMP_IMAGE`|no|
|`--image-pull-policy`|Pull policy for temporary PVC helper Pods; choices: `Always, IfNotPresent, Never`|`IfNotPresent`|`$KUBE_DUMP_IMAGE_PULL_POLICY`|no|
|`--helper-binary-path`|Path to the volume agent inside the helper container; default: kube-dump from PATH, then /kube-dump||`$KUBE_DUMP_HELPER_BINARY_PATH`|no|
|`--strategy`|PVC data acquisition strategy; choices: `pod, snapshot-copy`|`snapshot-copy`|`$KUBE_DUMP_STRATEGY`|no|
|`--concurrency`|Maximum parallel PVC backup lifecycles|`4`|`$KUBE_DUMP_CONCURRENCY`|no|
|`--snapshot-class`|VolumeSnapshotClass for snapshot-based strategies||`$KUBE_DUMP_SNAPSHOT_CLASS`|no|
|`--compression`|Compression for portable PVC data; choices: `zstd, gzip`|`zstd`|`$KUBE_DUMP_COMPRESSION`|no|
|`-n`, `--namespace`|Limit PVC data backup to these namespaces||`$KUBE_DUMP_NAMESPACE` (`,`)|no|
|`--pvc`|PVC name or glob pattern; repeatable||`$KUBE_DUMP_PVC` (`,`)|no|
|`--max-size`|Skip an individual PVC above this size, for example 1GiB||`$KUBE_DUMP_MAX_SIZE`|no|
|`--max-namespace-size`|Skip PVC data in a namespace above this total, for example 10GiB||`$KUBE_DUMP_MAX_NAMESPACE_SIZE`|no|
|`--keep`|Keep this many latest artifacts for each PVC; 0 disables rotation|`5`|`$KUBE_DUMP_KEEP`|no|

#### Arguments

|Name|Description|Required|
|---|---|---|
|`PATH`|Destination directory|yes|

### resource

Capture and process Kubernetes object manifests

Collect selected Kubernetes objects into a directory or archive, read them as YAML, inspect them, and move or transform the resulting manifest set.

**Usage:** `kube-dump [OPTIONS] resource [resource-OPTIONS]`

#### Examples

```text
kube-dump resource save dir ./backup
```

#### Capture and process Kubernetes object manifests

|Option|Description|Default|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|`-K`, `--kubeconfig`|Use this kubeconfig file without changing the user's current context||`$KUBE_DUMP_KUBECONFIG`|no|
|`-C`, `--context`|Select this kubeconfig context without modifying the kubeconfig||`$KUBE_DUMP_CONTEXT`|no|
|`--burst`|Maximum temporary burst of Kubernetes API requests|`100`|`$KUBE_DUMP_BURST`|no|
|`-t`, `--timeout`|Timeout applied to each Kubernetes API request||`$KUBE_DUMP_TIMEOUT`|no|
|`--qps`|Average Kubernetes API request rate allowed by the client|`50`|`$KUBE_DUMP_QPS`|no|
|`-k`, `--insecure-skip-tls-verify`|Disable Kubernetes TLS certificate verification; use only for trusted endpoints|||no|

### resource save

Capture selected Kubernetes objects to stdout, files, or an archive

Collect selected Kubernetes objects, apply the selected profile, and write multi-document YAML to stdout or store canonical resource files or an archive.

**Usage:** `kube-dump [OPTIONS] resource [resource-OPTIONS] save [save-OPTIONS]`

#### Examples

```text
kube-dump resource save dir ./backup --profile backup
```

#### Selection

|Option|Description|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|
|`-L`, `--label-selector`|Include objects matching Kubernetes label selector syntax|`$KUBE_DUMP_LABEL_SELECTOR`|no|
|`--annotation-selector`|Include objects matching Kubernetes annotation selector syntax|`$KUBE_DUMP_ANNOTATION_SELECTOR`|no|
|`--exclude-annotation-selector`|Exclude objects matching this annotation selector|`$KUBE_DUMP_EXCLUDE_ANNOTATION_SELECTOR`|no|
|`-r`, `--resource`|Include resources by plural name, full GVR, or kubectl short name|`$KUBE_DUMP_RESOURCE`|no|
|`-n`, `--namespace`|Include only these namespaces|`$KUBE_DUMP_NAMESPACE`|no|
|`--exclude-namespace`|Exclude these namespaces from namespaced collection|`$KUBE_DUMP_EXCLUDE_NAMESPACE`|no|

#### Profile

|Option|Description|Default|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|`--profile-dir`|Directory containing global profiles||`$KUBE_DUMP_PROFILE_DIR`|no|
|`-p`, `--profile`|Profile name, builtin:name, global:name, or YAML file|`backup`|`$KUBE_DUMP_PROFILE`|no|

#### Encryption

|Option|Description|Default|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|`--identity-passphrase`|Passphrase for an encrypted SSH identity||`$KUBE_DUMP_IDENTITY_PASSPHRASE`|no|
|`--identity-passphrase-file`|Read the passphrase for an encrypted SSH identity from this file||`$KUBE_DUMP_IDENTITY_PASSPHRASE_FILE`|no|
|`-i`, `--identity`|Age identity file used to decrypt archives, fields, or keyrings||`$KUBE_DUMP_IDENTITY` (`,`)|no|
|`--field-encryption`|Algorithm for fields selected by profile rules; no keys means plaintext; choices: `age, aes-siv`|`age`|`$KUBE_DUMP_FIELD_ENCRYPTION`|no|
|`-R`, `--recipient`|Age recipient used for encryption||`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENT` (`,`)|no|
|`--recipients-file`|File containing age recipients||`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENTS_FILE` (`,`)|no|
|`--recipients-url`|HTTP or HTTPS URL containing age recipients||`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENTS_URL` (`,`)|no|
|`--recipient-github-user`|GitHub username whose public SSH keys provide age recipients||`$KUBE_DUMP_RECIPIENT_GITHUB_USER` (`,`)|no|

#### Collection

|Option|Description|Default|Environment|Required|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|`--strict`|Abort on discovery, permission, or collection errors||`$KUBE_DUMP_STRICT`|no|
|`--concurrency`|Maximum parallel Kubernetes resource requests|`4`|`$KUBE_DUMP_CONCURRENCY`|no|
|`--page-size`|Maximum objects returned by one Kubernetes list request|`500`|`$KUBE_DUMP_PAGE_SIZE`|no|

### resource save stdout

#### Examples

```text
kube-dump resource save stdout --profile backup | kubectl apply -f -
```
